claims.text: The unchanged (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a large reversible caloric response.
The unchanged alloy has poor fracture toughness and is susceptible to cracking.
A coarse-grained microstructure causes the unchanged alloy's poor fracture toughness and crack formation.
The proposed intervention is cold rolling followed by rapid annealing.
Cold rolling followed by rapid annealing can refine this alloy's grains into the nanometer regime.
Annealing below the onset of deleterious phase segregation can permit recrystallization while preserving phase composition.
Grain refinement will increase the density of grain boundaries.
The increased grain-boundary density will impede crack propagation.
The alloy's caloric response is underpinned by a reversible martensitic or magnetostructural phase transformation.
Interfaces in the refined microstructure can remain sufficiently intact to permit the reversible caloric phase transformation.
Grain refinement by the proposed treatment will produce Hall–Petch strengthening.
The increased grain-boundary density will blunt crack tips and thereby enhance toughness and load-bearing capacity.
The proposed treatment can maintain compositional uniformity and phase distribution sufficiently to avoid shifting or diminishing the caloric transition.
The processed alloy will have fewer and smaller cracks and greater fracture toughness or bending strength than the unchanged alloy.
The processed alloy will retain entropy change and field- or pressure-induced temperature changes comparable to those of the unchanged alloy.
Excessive annealing or cold work may disrupt the desired phase balance and compromise the proposed benefit.
The intended mechanical-integrity improvement is greater than 20% relative to the conventionally processed control.
